$comment: THE STRUCTURAL FINDING OF THIS HALF, and the reason the outer shadow is one
of the two fields that moved.
On macOS 26.5 the receded pose casts no outer shadow at all. That is a
measurement and not an assumption: the native 26.5 inactive cells read a mean
exterior departure of 0.00003 to 0.0001 over every backdrop and span, which is
zero at this instrument's resolution, and it is why W27c's endpoint zeroes all
eight of the block's amplitude leaves.
On macOS 27 it does. The same cells read 0.00119 at span 44, 0.00296 at 96,
0.00527 on the stack and 0.01002 at 160 — between a quarter and one and a half
times what the 27 ACTIVE pose casts at the same span. So the 27 receded
document does not zero the block: it carries its own active document's shadow,
leaf for leaf, and the read says that is right. Against the eight identified
inactive cells the departure residual is 0.00045 mean absolute at a signed mean
of +0.00009, which is the shadow axis's own noise floor on this bed.
Recorded as a difference in WHAT THE RECEDE IS rather than as a tuning: on
26.5 the pose removes the material's elevation and on 27 it keeps it.

theTintShade: `tintShadeDark` 0.0288 and `tintShadeLight` 0.76 do NOT move, and the residual
they leave is named rather than absorbed.
The six tinted light inactive calibration cells read +0.066 at the darkest
backdrop, +0.048 over `dark-solid`, +0.040 and +0.023 over the photograph,
+0.028 over the checkerboard and -0.005 over `light-solid` — a residual that
falls monotonically with the untinted body's own level and changes sign at the
bright end. The shade law is `mix(tintShadeDark, tintShadeLight, u)` in exactly
that level, and a least squares over the five untinted/tinted pairs returns a
NEGATIVE dark end (-0.060), which the law cannot represent: clamped at zero it
trades +0.066 at the dark end for -0.029 at the bright one and improves no
cell's worst case. So the 27 receded tint is not linear in the body level over
this range, which is a model-form gap and not a tuning residual, and this child
leaves the constants where W28 fitted them and records the gap.
theRim: `rimCollapsedTinted` stay at zero. §5.151 §8 measured the 27 recede taking
away LESS rim than the 26.5 recede (contour rim -0.067 against -0.110), which
reads like a reason to restore some — and the bed says not to. The 27 ACTIVE
rim is itself a fifth of the 26.5 one (§5.153 §2 item 2), so removing all of a
much smaller rim already lands in the right place: against the eighteen
identified inactive cells the radial rim peak residual is 0.0032 mean absolute,
and where it is worst it is vitrea drawing MORE rim than the reference
(+0.0196 on the dark `light-solid` capsule), which restoring rim would make
worse. The recede's rim delta moved; the rim it leaves behind did not.

method: The anchors move to the 27 ACTIVE document's, [0.004, 0.11, 0.425, 0.95],
and that is the load-bearing half of this fit. W28's anchors start at 0.1104
because the 26.5 bed's uniform backdrops start there; the 27 active refit
moved the first knot to the darkest backdrop there is (§5.153 §2 item 1) and
the recede has to follow it. While it did not, every cell over `impulse`
clamped to an ordinate no cell identified and rendered 0.4612 against a
reference of 0.2323 — a fifth of the whole residual, on two cells, and
immovable by any value of that ordinate. Re-anchoring alone took the bed-wide
residual from 0.0433 to 0.0213.
The ordinates are then the native inactive level read at each anchor, because
the rendered level tracks the response ordinate to within 0.02 on this
material: 0.2823 over `dark-solid`, 0.4955-0.4975 over the photograph, 0.8310
over `light-solid`. Two iterations of the residual close the rest.
The 27 light recede is nearly THICKNESS-INDEPENDENT, which the 26.5 one is
not: its thin and thick rows differ by 0.44 at the dark anchor (0.0126 against
0.4553) and by 0.02 here. That is the same convergence §5.153 §2 found in the
active light document, arriving in the pose.

backdropToneResponse.status: measured and fitted, with the dark anchor at a floor
method: The anchors move to the 27 active dark document's, [0.004, 0.11, 0.47, 0.95],
for the light document's reason. The third knot is 0.47 and not 0.425 because
that is where the 27 active dark refit put it.
The far ordinate is the largest move on this bed and it is fitted on a
CALIBRATION cell, which its 26.5 predecessor never was: W27c G1c refused the
measured value for want of a uniform anchor and W27c G1d adopted 0.9326072
from the 140/255 probe. On 27 `light-solid__capsule-button__inactive` is a
dark calibration cell and reads 0.4419, so the ordinate is 0.448 and the
residual on it is -0.0003. The dark recede over a bright backdrop is half what
the 26.5 endpoint drew.
**The dark anchor is a floor, not a fit.** The bed's cell there is
`impulse__capsule-button__inactive`, which is VALIDATION on this profile, and
the residual is one-signed and immovable: at ordinate 0.09 the web renders
0.0893 against a reference of 0.0105, at 0.0105 it renders 0.0654 and at 0
it renders 0.0580. Driving the ordinate to the bottom of its range buys the
last 0.007 and leaves +0.0475. So something other than the response holds the
27 dark recede's floor over a near-black backdrop about 0.058 above the
reference, and this document records that rather than pretending the constant
is fitted. The thick row takes the same 0 for the same reason and has no
cell of its own there at all.
